input.text: Welcome to Panjiayuan — Beijing's greatest treasure hunt, and the largest antique and crafts market of its kind in China. What began as a spontaneous "dirt market" — vendors spreading their wares on the ground before dawn — is now a city block of thousands of stalls: Mao-era memorabilia, porcelain, jade, seals, faded family photos, Buddhist statues, lamps, lacquer, and things no category can hold. The unwritten rule: much of what you'll see is old-styled rather than old — so browse for beauty, bargain with humor, and never buy what you can't afford to love as a replica. The market's soul is the weekend: vendors arrive before sunrise, and serious hunters come with flashlights. Prices start high and drop with a smile and a walk-away — halving the first quote is normal. Bring cash-sized patience and small bills, keep your valuables front, and give yourself two hours. Everything here has a story — and half the fun is the vendor telling it.
